eligibility_reason: Section 4.2 (p. 4) defines episodic memory M_ep: each agent node's successful subgoal trajectory is recorded as an experience tuple (t_e, v_e, s_e) and 'gradually expanded through successful runs'; at inference an agent node retrieves the top-k most similar past experiences by cosine similarity over sentence embeddings of the current subgoal. The same section defines working memory, a shared store 'automatically updated whenever an agent observes movable objects during interaction' and read back later via an explicit 'recall location of <object>' action. Both are agent-written, run-time stores queried on later turns/episodes to condition behaviour, satisfying I1. Year 2025/2026 (AAMAS 2026, p. 1) satisfies I2; English text and retrievable pages satisfy I3/I4. No exclusion applies: the store is not fixed (E3 does not hold, since episodic memory is 'gradually augmented with additional successful executions', p. 4) and memory is a named, evaluated contribution rather than incidental (contribution (2) on p. 2; ablations in Table 1, p. 5).

facets.justification: p. 4: episodic memory stores sentence embeddings v_e = f_sen(g_e) of each recorded experience and retrieves via cosine similarity sim(v_n, v_e) over the stored embeddings.

p. 4: 'Episodic memory M_ep stores experiences from agent nodes involved in task executions that ultimately succeed... episodic memory can be bootstrapped from a few manually collected trajectories and gradually augmented with additional successful executions.' Each experience is stored as-is (the raw trajectory tuple); nothing already stored is rewritten or condensed.
p. 4: the agent embeds its current subgoal and 'retrieves the top k similar experiences (with k determined by a token limit) as in-context examples,' via cosine similarity.

p. 5 (Table 1) and p. 1 (abstract): evaluated on the WAH-NL and ALFRED benchmarks against five baselines across seven LLMs, with ablations on memory systems and control flow. No deployed setting or real users are reported anywhere in the given pages.

p. 5: Table 1 reports goal success rate (GSR) and subgoal success rate (SSR) for ReAcTree/ReAcTree+WM against five baselines over a fixed task suite (WAH-NL, ALFRED), the defining pattern of benchmark_evaluation.

p. 2, contributions list item (1): 'ReAcTree, a hierarchical planning framework... where each agent node independently solves a subgoal while control flow nodes coordinate their execution into a coherent plan' — an architecture combining an agent tree, control-flow nodes, and two memory systems, not a single algorithmic technique.
